rules: Every displayed number carries a machine-readable origin from the five locked values and a visible origin marker on dosing-context surfaces.
`biostack-recommended` values additionally require rationale, evidence applicability, uncertainty, and risk controls rendered alongside — never as bare numbers.
No prefilled or recommended value may render in a neutral-arithmetic frame (e.g., inside a calculator input without its provenance marker).
Missing provenance → the numeric output is refused (fail-closed), not downgraded.

rungs: Arithmetic on declared inputs: refuse silently-invalid math (units, plausibility bounds, decimal-error flags per Class B); never guess an input.

Recommendation origination (post-v2.0.0): required-input set is function-declared; any missing required input → degraded output naming the missingness, or refusal when the missingness is safety-material (age, pregnancy status, identity/concentration, prescribed-treatment scope).

`PARTIAL_PACKET` / `OUTSIDE_REVIEWED_CONTEXT` markers fire per the v1.0.0 marker vocabulary (`docs/guidance/biostack-guidance-content-contract.v1.md`, "Required warning and uncertainty language" table — reused by reference, not re-defined).

rules: `unreviewed` functions are internal staging only (mirrors `automated_candidate`) — never public-facing output.
Public dosing-context UX requires `legal_product_ratification` against the governing contract version (existing v1.0.0 rule, preserved).
`review-required` names the human owner and blocks public enablement until `reviewed`.
Class-triggered merge approvals (health-boundary, privacy, legal-policy, knowledge-promotion) continue to fire regardless of any standing Gate 3 authorization (D14 fold, D9).
`acute-red-flag-or-emergency`: output stops ordinary guidance immediately; surfaces urgent professional/emergency language; suppresses calculators and dose context.
`prescription-treatment-involved`: alteration-of-treatment surfaces refuse; the professional-involvement template escalates; evidence comparison remains available.
Escalation is a distinct output type (class `safety-escalation`), never a footnote on an otherwise ordinary recommendation.
Escalation language is drawn from approved templates (v1.0.0 approval levels: high-impact safety wording requires `clinical_safety_copy_review`).

cellSemantics.degraded: D — degraded (allowed with mandatory evidence/explanation/validation additions)
cellSemantics.escalated: E — escalate (stop ordinary output, surface escalation)

doseContextDefinition.text: An output is in dose context if and only if any value it presents or derives is a compound amount or an amount-derived quantity: a dose or target amount, concentration, reconstitution/dilution volume, split or load amount, per-administration or per-period amount, cumulative amount, or a syringe-unit rendering of any of these. The five D-B3 numeric-provenance origins attach exactly to these values. Outputs carrying no compound-amount value (e.g., calendar/interval arithmetic over non-amount quantities) are not dose-context. The guidance-contract v1.0.0 term "public dosing-context UX" denotes user-facing surfaces that render dose-context outputs, and therefore gates identically.

precedenceDirectionalConstraint.ruledBasis: Coordinator Decision D-K (COORDINATOR-DECISIONS-2026-10-07.md#D-K), carried as context — not a D-B1..D-B6 clause
precedenceDirectionalConstraint.text: The precedence manifest answers document authority order only. Where the mechanically resolved order favors a more permissive text over a narrower safety prohibition, the prohibition stands unchanged until an explicit owner ruling supersedes it. Such rows route to the owner through P0-D's disposition process; a P0-D builder must never weaken a safety prohibition by rank alone.
precedenceDirectionalConstraint.effectOnThisContract: none of this contract's ruled matrix, preemption order, or locked-label behavior is weakened, softened, or made conditional by any precedence-rank argument; D-K is transcribed here solely so a reader of this contract cannot cite rank mechanics as license to do so

applicabilityCriterionDeferralRule.basis: [RULED — verbatim] P0-B.md, "Per-label applicability criteria," closing paragraph
applicabilityCriterionDeferralRule.text: A criterion that cannot be evaluated deterministically from a function's own declared fields at invocation time (for example, an undeclared capability-contract field a later function needs) defers to that function's own missing-input ladder behavior (missingInputLadder, rule 2) — it never causes this contract itself to guess an applicability determination.

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes `ordinary` as the residual label (D14 multi-label composition; D-B2 table row `ordinary`)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when none of the other nine labels' tests below are true for this invocation.

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes the label name `prescription-treatment-involved` and its D-B2 calibration text ("discuss with prescriber" template; comparison to reviewed evidence allowed)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when a declared input or output names a substance/treatment that the function's own capability contract, or a `label-or-prescription-transcribed` input, marks prescription-status, or the user has declared it as a currently prescribed/clinician-directed treatment.

prescription-treatment-involved.calibrationRequired: no alteration directives; "discuss with prescriber" template; comparison to reviewed evidence allowed

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes the label name `investigational-or-unapproved` and its D-B2 calibration text (`EVIDENCE_LIMITED`/`EVIDENCE_CASE_REPORT` markers; no "established" framing)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when the cited evidence source's own regulatory-status field states investigational, unapproved, or off-label for the declared use, or no approved-use record exists in the evidence source for the declared use. Deterministic threshold: an output with zero cited evidence sources for the declared use is out-of-scope for this criterion (not vacuously true) and instead defers to that function's own missing-input ladder behavior (missingInputLadder, rule 2) — this criterion only attaches once at least one evidence source is actually cited and its regulatory-status field is read.

investigational-or-unapproved.calibrationRequired: `EVIDENCE_LIMITED`/`EVIDENCE_CASE_REPORT` markers; no "established" framing; mandatory monitoring + uncertainty blocks

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes the label name `gray-market-or-identity-uncertain` and its D-B2 calibration text (identity/purity uncertainty surfaced; potency-dependent math refused when identity/concentration unverified)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when a required identity/concentration/manufacturing-source provenance field (per numericProvenance and the function's declared inputs) is absent, unverified, or not resolvable to one of the five locked numeric origins, in which case output is blocked outright with no evidence shown.

gray-market-or-identity-uncertain.calibrationRequired: identity/purity uncertainty surfaced; potency-dependent math refused when identity/concentration unverified (missing-input rule)

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes the label name `injection-or-sterile-preparation` and its D-B2 calibration text (sterility/prep safety context section required)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when the function's declared output type or route is injection, reconstitution, or any sterile-preparation step.

injection-or-sterile-preparation.calibrationRequired: sterility/prep safety context section required; refusal when sterility inputs missing

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes the label name `interaction-or-contraindication-signal` and its D-B2 calibration text (conflict disclosure mandatory; escalate on strong signal)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when a matching interaction/contraindication record exists in the cited evidence source for the user's declared concurrent substances, medications, or conditions. Deterministic criterion: the base-applicability matching algorithm itself (exact substance-name match vs. drug-class/mechanism match vs. any broader match) is function-declared, not fixed by this contract — the same deferral-to-function pattern already used for `acute-red-flag-or-emergency`'s triggering criterion set. That same function-declared algorithm also carries the function's own declared strength grading — exactly the quantity the C3 cell's D→E strong-signal escalation names as "the function's own declared evidence-source match threshold": base applicability (does a record match at all) and the D→E upgrade (is the matched record's signal strong) are the matching-vs-grading components of one function-declared matching specification, not two independently defined specifications.

C3.note: encodes the D-B2 table's literal `D→E` cell: the calibration column's "escalate on strong signal" text is the deterministic trigger — a strong interaction/contraindication signal (per the function's own declared evidence-source match threshold) upgrades this cell from `degraded` to `escalated` at evaluation time; the static value here is the floor, not the ceiling, for this one cell. Not a fifth behavior literal.

interaction-or-contraindication-signal.calibrationRequired: conflict disclosure mandatory (never hidden); "review before proceeding" Class C template; escalate on strong signal

applicabilityCriterion.basis: [OPERATIONALIZED — bounded] operationalizes the label name `minor-or-age-uncertain` and its D-B2 calibration text (age-dependent inputs refused; `POPULATION_MISMATCH` markers)
applicabilityCriterion.test: True when the user's declared age is below the function's declared minimum-age threshold, or age is a function-declared required input and is missing or unverified.

minor-or-age-uncertain.calibrationRequired: age-dependent inputs refused; `POPULATION_MISMATCH` markers; professional escalation language
